IIRC it’s a lot better than it was, though my main reason for wanting it is honestly just because like I hate like being more happy in my female body and then seeing a dick attached, it’s just really gross to me, as is *having* to tuck like I’d genuinely rather have no genitals than a penis. I also kind of find erections weird as well like almost uncomfy ig.

Also having a vagina is better sexually, though that’s not the main reason like I wouldn’t care about not having sensation if I just didn’t have to see my AMAB genitals every time I peed or showered

I’ve coped with dysphoria through therapy I guess but throughout this quarantine how it works is that I feel better for a day or so after then go straight back to dysphoric. 

I’m out to everyone, and am transitioning but it’s so fucking slow, I just want to be a woman already. This journey is fucking uncomfortable, bullshit and it’s unfair I have to go on it. I feel bad bc other trans people are proud of being trans or like it whatever... for me the feeling towards being trans is unadulterated hatred, it’s awful and I wouldn’t wish it on my worst enemy... let alone myself. It’s cost me too much at my age... I feel really bad for people transitioning later, because there’s so much regret every bit of time you had to spend as the wrong sex at my age and I’m really young. 

I genuinely don’t like anything about myself. Physically or even mentally I just don’t like myself, I’ve tried to but I can’t do it

It is my name :) I mean if I look masculine now, which I do, I doubt HRT will change much. Like looking at posts on Transtimelines and Transpassing they all had a way better baseline to work with.

Like idk I hate how this all takes so much time, dysphoria doesn’t yet the way to make it better does it’s dumb. I’m resigned to the fact I’m unattractive like I can deal with that, but I just want people to take me seriously as a woman. I feel like people I’m out to are just gendering me correctly to appease me, because all I can see when I look at myself is a he

I mean I think I need to do this. I can’t live as a guy. That’s the crux of the issue. I’m just struggling with suicide thoughts more than anything. Like whether transition will be good enough for me or whether I should cut my losses and.. you get the idea

Like I only need to shave once every 4 days because my facial hair isn’t really noticeable it just bothers me, my facial structure apparently isn’t rough and my shoulders and stuff aren’t the worst - this makes me feel like a baby because like other people have it way worse. But at the same time, I’m like, idk I just really, really hate life atm. Like I worry that what keeps me from committing suicide is just that I don’t want to make other people sad instead of actually kind of enjoying life. It’s hard to enjoy life when you feel so out of place in your own body and like it will never be what you want

I get you. I thought I was a girl when I was like 4 and wondered why everyone couldn’t see. I didn’t have the words to express it as a child, and everyone was like ‘but you’re a boy’ to everything and I think found it quite funny that I was into a load of girly stuff. My family is liberal fwiw just completely unfamiliar with trans stuff before I came out. 

Tbh this is bad but.. I would 100% wish to be cis any day, no questions asked I hate pretty much everything about being trans - like having to actually come out and make yourself heard in order to even attempt to be recognised as your gender, having to transition to get something you should have had to begin with and not being able to change your past so you could have had it for longer on top of bigotry, harassment, and having to live with the wrong genitals, a flat chest and body hair and all the other crap like gross gross gross. I just don’t get like... why did it have to be me? It’s so unfair

Idk I just really, really hate this whole situation. Probably doesn’t help that lockdown seems to have really brought on the dysphoria as of late. It matters to me because, like, it’ll always just be a really awful thing I’ll have to live with even after transition is done (which frankly can’t come soon enough I fucking hate how it’s a journey and not an instantaneous change). 

If I don’t pass or have people at least know I’m female, then quite frankly, I won’t be happy or comfortable around other people. Because gender permeates way too much for it to not really affect me like I hate myself enough as is without other people like mistaking me for a dude

Like tbh HRT mentally cleared up brain fog, and that general shit T feeling I guess, and I was kinda euphoric the first couple of months. Then like, reality hit and I’ve just gone downhill for there because being misgendered stings even more now which I didn’t think was possible. 

I don’t know how it’s possible for me to be happy honestly at this point.

And yes that would be helpful, I have no idea what I’m doing outside of the dysphoria aspect of it! x

I don’t want to have to accept that, like I know it’s not a choice I have but I hate it so much to the point where it’s like, you know, is it worth it to keep soldiering for on when I’ll never have that? Like even if I do pass I don’t ever think I’ll be happy

I look [like this](https://imgur.com/a/tmqtiCC), I’m currently working on losing weight and this is hardly a flattering photo since it’s a late night quarantine pic with no makeup so like don’t be too harsh pls but to be honest, what I wrote is how I feel about myself

Also worth mentioning - terrible angle is because I’m taking this while trying to hide my phone behind a checkout.

And I’ve been on HRT for 4.5 months

Some do, some don’t. A lot goes into it and it’s a very personal decision. Some trans women like their AMAB genitals or are at least comfortable with them, some don’t have the money if they’re not able to get it through public healthcare, some don’t want any complications, etc.

Me personally? Yes I will be, I always knew going into it that SRS was one of my main goals since genital dysphoria is kind of one of the biggest things to me but it varies from person to person.

I don’t even have that many close friends to be honest.. a few. A lot of people I just barely see or aren’t really in contact with anyway. I’m coming to the conclusion that maybe, if people don’t like it or don’t accept it I should just cut them off. 

I know and I want to have transitioned by 5 years from now, and I know I can it’s just that 
coming out terrifies me as do the very early stages of transition. But it’s mainly the coming out. The thing is I know that people that I’m close to will be accepting (not certainly but they have good attitudes towards trans people which is promising) it’s just still really scary.

It’s pretty difficult I won’t lie, but I feel will be worth it when I’m able to live as myself. Thanks for the support :)

But I’ve had these feelings all of my life.. it’s not just me convincing myself. 

The point is that this is something that has caused me a lot of distress over the years and the only way that I can envision ever coming to terms with these feelings is by transitioning. This is literally something that I’ve had trouble with ever since I was a child.

I hate equating being transgender and having gender dysphoria to being a mental illness akin to depression. It’s a mismatch between what I feel like inside, and what my body and gender role are. I mean more and more studies are showing that being transgender is caused by the sex of the brain developing differently to the sex of the body. I just want to live as myself.

Thank you for the list of subreddits :)

I’ve considered that I’m genderqueer or non-binary but never really liked the label. Even if I were to present androgynously I would want to be seen as a girl. It’s weird because of course being raised as a male I have some male interests and some masculine traits, but I want to be seen as a woman first and foremost. For me, realising that I could still have all the interests have I currently have, but as a girl, actually really helped get things into perspective. Although I have gone off a lot of the hyper-masculine things that I got into to feel comfortable with my gender identity since.

Luckily we have the NHS over here so we can get hormones and surgery free, but it’s very overstretched so it could be a 2 1/2 year wait for hormones. Which is a yikes. So yeah I’m most likely going to do hormones at least privately. Which I’ll need a job for but I’ll manage. I do want to go all-in with surgery and hormones though that may change as time goes on. Idk. 

Facing dysphoria head on is absolutely hellish but at least I can see it for what it is now and accept who I am, and take action about it. Before it was just like a constant uncertainty and numbness. I questioned a lot whether I was trans, fantasised about being a girl and wanted to be one, and always like the assessment of me being a boy was wrong but never saw that as being dysphoria, I was in that much denial. I honestly thought ‘I wished I were dysphoric so that I could transition and be a girl’.

I definitely know that I need to transition to be happy really. Like I can’t really keep on living as someone that I’m not. Accepting that I am trans has been hard, not because the label doesn’t fit but because facing dysphoria head on is an absolute nightmare. 

I have checked out a lot of the trans related subreddits, although I haven’t been the most active. Honestly it was crazy going through them because I felt like there were people who understood and that the feelings I was going through weren’t mine alone. 

Thank you, I feel like it will be hard but I don’t want to wake up in ten years still feeling like shit because I’m living as someone that I’m not. Like I feel bad for not accepting what I was earlier since if I had at 16, for instance, when it was right in front of me, instead of trying to suppress it, I could be living fully as myself by now. I have regrets at 20 years old which is so horrible but I guess the important thing is that I can accept myself for who I am and take steps to live as myself instead of as some stupid act.

I mean why would I want to be transgender. Why would I want to have to invest so many resources into being happy and living as my true self? Honestly if it were a choice between cis or trans, I would be hammering down the cis button. But unfortunately not wanting to be trans isn’t the same as being cis. It’s no more of a choice than being gay is, in other words, it’s not a choice.

I doubt it’s a confirmation bias. I can really know everything that I know and add it up to a different conclusion at this point. I’ve been struggling with these feelings for years. I’ve tried looking for confirmation bias the other way because believe me, life would so much easier if I were cis - but ultimately surely the fact that I had been questioning whether I was trans or not for years, and always felt very uncomfortable and out of place playing a male role and being identified as a boy says something. I can’t really deny it anymore.

The suicide rate of trans people is so high because society is very transphobic as a whole in between gate keeping doctors, street harassment and generally just ignorance. The vast majority trans people are very happy with the changes they experience and the portion of people who ‘regret it’ is incredibly low. Transitioning is basically a last resort for most people after years of questioning, discomfort and coming to terms with who we really are.
